chunk_findings.detail: `_auto_sync_on_claim` only sets `wt.sync_note` when the automatic-sync outcome has `status == "conflict"`. The `auto_sync` contract in `sync.py` says a `refused` outcome also leaves the tree as it was and “says why” (for example, when `[worktree] auto_sync_refuse_on_conflict` is enabled and the merge/rebase would conflict). For that outcome the claim sets no note, so the claim can succeed with an empty `sync_warn` and start the item on an unsynced tree, silently leaving the gate baseline problem this change is meant to report.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim.py:_auto_sync_on_claim

chunk_findings.detail: `usable()` only rejects a tree whose resolved path equals the resolved `repo` path. Git commands run with `tree` as the working directory affect the containing worktree, so a path inside the primary checkout passes the guard: with `repo = Path("/repo")` and `tree = Path("/repo/ddflow")`, `is_primary()` returns False because the paths differ, `git -C /repo/ddflow rev-parse --git-dir` succeeds, and `usable()` returns True. Auto-sync can then run `git -C /repo/ddflow merge main` or `rebase main`, modifying the primary checkout despite the stated “never touches the primary checkout” invariant. The check should use the worktree top-level (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`) or otherwise ensure `tree` is not inside the primary checkout.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/autosync.py:usable/is_primary

chunk_findings.detail: When a rebase fails with conflicts and `git rebase --abort` also fails, `_failed_rebase()` records `out.aborted = False` and returns a conflict/refused status. `autosync.blocks()` ignores `aborted` and only stops the gate for `status == "conflict"` when `auto_sync_refuse_on_conflict` is true. Thus, with that knob false (or when `files` is empty and the status is `refused`), `before_gate` can start gates in a worktree that `_failed_rebase()` itself says may be left mid-rebase. A failed abort should block the gate regardless of the conflict-refusal setting.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/branchsync.py:_failed_rebase

chunk_findings.detail: The guard “never when one of them has already passed” only checks `r.outcome == "passed"` and never checks that the passed gate record names the current tree/commit. Gate records are historical (the gates code already has `_recorded_since` for commit-aware checks), so a stale pass can suppress auto-sync. For example, if `ci` passed on commit A, the lane later gets new commits making the current tree B, and main has moved past the old merge-base, a subsequent `unit_tests` gate start sees `it.gates["ci"].outcome == "passed"` and returns `None` before calling `auto_sync`. `unit_tests` then runs on a tree based on the old base, contrary to the stated behavior that a waiting item’s worktree is brought up to main before a gate starts and contrary to the docstring’s own “a pass names a commit” condition.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates/_autosync.py:before_gate

chunk_findings.detail: `_auto_sync_on_claim` only surfaces an auto-sync problem when `got.data.get("status") == "conflict"`. The `auto_sync` outcome documented in `sync.py` also has a `refused` status for a sync that was blocked because of a conflict (`refuse_on_conflict`), and it says the tree was left as it was. If a claim runs with `auto_sync_refuse_on_conflict` enabled and the existing worktree merge/rebase conflicts, `auto_sync` can return `status == "refused"`, the helper leaves `wt.sync_note` unset, and the claim succeeds with no `sync_warn`/note that the worktree was not brought up to date. That lets the user proceed believing the auto-sync reported the conflict, violating the intent that conflicts are reported and never silently ignored.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim.py:_auto_sync_on_claim

chunk_findings.detail: When a worktree is checked out at an older commit of `base` and has no unique commits, `HEAD` is an ancestor of the current `base` tip. For that input, `tip != head`, so the function reaches `merge-base`, which returns `head`. The final condition treats `mb.out in (tip, head)` as “measure `base`’s tip” and returns `""`. A baseline comparison that uses an empty result as “use current base tip” therefore compares the old worktree against the moved main, exactly the B1c1e1c9213 failure mode: failures that exist at the worktree’s actual base but were fixed or changed on main are attributed to the lane. The function should return the merge-base (`head`) whenever the tree does not contain the current base tip, even if the tree has no unique commits, unless it can specifically identify a finished/merged item.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/autosync.py:fork_point

chunk_findings.detail: `_failed_rebase` runs `git rebase --abort` whenever `git rebase` returns non-zero, without any way to know whether the failed rebase was the one started by this `sync()` call. If the worktree already has a rebase in progress (for example the user is mid-interactive-rebase, or a previous operation left `.git/rebase-apply`), then `sync(..., strategy="rebase")` runs `git rebase rep.base`, git fails with “already rebase in progress”, and `_failed_rebase` aborts the user’s pre-existing rebase. That destroys the user’s rebase state and auto-resolves an in-progress operation, contrary to the stated “never touches” / “conflicts are reported, never auto-resolved” behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/branchsync.py:_failed_rebase

chunk_findings.detail: When `git rebase` fails before a rebase is actually created, the handler still tries `git rebase --abort` and, if that fails, appends a warning that the tree “may be left mid-rebase”. For example, if the worktree has an untracked file that the base branch also adds, `git rebase main` fails before starting a rebase; `git rebase --abort` then fails with “No rebase in progress”, and the result falsely tells the user to run `git rebase --abort` by hand because the tree may be mid-rebase, even though no rebase was in progress.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/branchsync.py:_failed_rebase

chunk_findings.detail: `blocks` only stops a gate for `status == "conflict"`, but the same change now treats `status == "refused"` as an auto-sync problem that must be surfaced in `ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim.py:_auto_sync_on_claim`, and the documented `refused` outcome can represent a conflicted sync that was left as it was because `refuse_on_conflict` was enabled. Given `auto_sync_refuse_on_conflict=true` and a waiting worktree whose merge/rebase conflicts, if `auto_sync` returns `{"status": "refused", "aborted": True}`, `_autosync.before_gate` calls `blocks(cfg, "refused", True)`, which returns `False`; the gate therefore starts on a tree that the sync deliberately refused to bring up to date, defeating the gate-side part of `refuse_on_conflict`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/autosync.py:blocks

chunk_findings.detail: The new guard only avoids `git rebase --abort` when `_rebasing(tree)` is exactly `False`. If a user or another process starts a rebase in the same worktree after `_unsafe` has passed its `_rebasing` check but before the auto-sync `git rebase` command actually runs, the auto-sync rebase fails because Git sees an existing rebase. `_failed_rebase` then sees `_rebasing(tree) is True` — the *other* rebase’s state — and runs `git rebase --abort`, destroying that in-progress rebase. This contradicts the intended/tested behavior that a rebase already in progress is never aborted and can lose the user’s rebase state.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/branchsync.py:_failed_rebase

chunk_findings.detail: The line `(wt / ".git").exists()  # a linked worktree: .git is a file` is a bare expression, not an assertion, so the linked-worktree precondition it comments on is never checked. If `_claimed(repo)` returned the primary checkout (or a non-linked tree), the test would still create `rebase-merge` under that tree's git directory and could pass the later refusal assertions, so this test would not catch a regression that touches the primary checkout.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_auto_sync_main.py:test_a_rebase_already_in_progress_is_never_aborted_and_a_refusal_aborts_nothing
